content: 1. A liquid heated intentionally to a temperature of 100°F (38°C) or higher and transported at or above its flash point in bulk packaging is subject to specific regulations. 2. A liquid with a flash point of 115.5°C (141°F) or higher, constituting at least 99% of the total volume of a mixture, is regulated differently if it is not transported at or above its flash point. 3. Any liquid with a flash point greater than 35°C (95°F) that does not sustain combustion, as determined by ASTM 4206 or the procedure outlined in Appendix H, is not classified as a flammable liquid. 4. A liquid with a flash point greater than 35°C (95°F) and a fire point exceeding 100°C (212°F), as determined by ISO 2592, is also not classified as a flammable liquid. 5. A liquid with a flash point greater than 35°C (95°F) that is part of a water-miscible solution with a water content exceeding 90% by mass is not considered a flammable liquid. 6. The flash point is defined as the minimum temperature at which a liquid emits sufficient vapor within a test vessel to form an ignitable mixture with air near the liquid's surface. 7. A flammable liquid with a flash point at or above 38°C (100°F) that does not meet the criteria for any other hazard class may be reclassified as a combustible liquid. 8. This reclassification does not apply to transportation by vessel or aircraft unless other means of transportation are impractical. 9. A material intentionally heated and transported at or above its flash point, meeting the definition of a Class 3 material, cannot be reclassified as a combustible liquid. 10. A combustible liquid that does not sustain combustion is not subject to the requirements of this subchapter as a combustible liquid. 11. The test method specified in ASTM 4206 or the procedure in Appendix H may be used to determine whether a material sustains combustion when heated under test conditions and exposed to an external flame source. 12. Gasoline: An alternative placard may be used for gasoline transported in non-bulk quantities. 13. Fuel Oil: An alternative placard may be used for fuel oil transported in non-bulk quantities.
